title: Dense FP64 projection
description: The plain projection every projections plugin is compared with: y = W x with exact sums. On the device, a BF16 matrix multiplied by torch.

projections.about: dense weight formats and their GEMM/GEMV kernels, with fused epilogues

host.prepare: prepare(rows) -> weight: a dense [out][in] matrix in the plugin's format
host.dense: dense(weight) -> rows: the values project multiplies with (the format's decoded matrix)

device.load: load(tensors, format, role=None, encode=None) -> matrix: a matrix on the device from a checkpoint's stored tensors; format is the encoding (bf16, fp8:channel, fp8:tensor, mxfp8, nvfp4; a plugin refuses one it does not take), tensors as stored ({weight, scale, global_scale, input_scale} by role); role, where the model plugin gives one, is the matrix's part in the model in the model's own words (qkv, gate_up, ...), which a plugin may choose its arithmetic by; encode, which the model plugin passes only for a matrix only a drafter reads, names a format the plugin re-encodes the stored one to (nvfp4, fp8), recorded in its facts (draft_encoding)
device.matmul: matmul(x, matrix, out_dtype=None) -> y: y[t] = W x[t] for each token row of x ([tokens][in], the activation dtype); in a call of up to invariant_rows(plugin) rows (decode rows, verify windows: DECODE_ROWS, or the facts' row_invariance rows when more) every row's bits are those of the row alone, so batched decoding matches serial; a longer call (prompt rows) may sum in another order than a shorter one, unless the plugin's facts say row_invariance prompt_rows (then a row's bits are the same in any call of more than invariant_rows(plugin) rows); out_dtype asks for the output in a dtype of its own (FP32 for logits) from the same FP32 sums
